glbs: assets/source/roster/<family>/ as committed at 2a68e25d7 (the spec commit); probed tier 0 in vehicle mode (wheels and tracks kept, dressing_* skipped)

convention.hull_box: reaches the hull and turret roof; where a bulky sight stands more than the 0.3 m bulky dressing allowance over the roof, the top is the sight's top less 0.3 m (decisions.md F-B1)
convention.pivot: centre of the turret ring; for a fixed mount, the point it is drawn hinged on (only pivot + muzzle reaches the simulation)
convention.muzzle: pivot_m + muzzle_m at rest, at the real barrel or launch point
convention.frame: hull box centred on x = 0 and y = 0, standing on z = 0; +x forward, +y left

thresholds.hull_dimension: fix when off by more than max(0.10 m, 3 %)
thresholds.pivot_x: fix when off by more than 0.15 m
thresholds.muzzle_point: fix when the world muzzle point is off by more than 0.15 m on any axis (added by lane F-B, decisions.md F-B3)
thresholds.eye_m: kept unless a source contradicts it; nothing measured here does

sources.note: nose right, launcher and radar raised. Hull 1391 px. The turret (radar at the front, launcher behind it) spans 0.43 to 1.03 of the hull length from the tail; its base box centres at 0.73. Rear drive sprocket, engine deck behind the turret
confirms the layout: a low engine deck at the rear, the turret forward with the radar facing forward, the launcher hinged at the turret's rear

9A317 TELAR 8.0 x 3.3 x 3.8 m; the same figure is repeated for most vehicles of the system, so it is weak. Other sources give 9.3 x 3.25 x 3.8 m for the M1/M2 TELAR; none was found for the M3's 9A317M

verdicts.note: No trustworthy published dimension; the photos have no scale. But 9.75 m is past the tracked cap (4.8 m half-length), which matters once the mobility is fixed (see findings); 9.3 m is the best-supported figure then

The frame and the art put the turret at the rear behind a cab; the real TELAR's turret stands forward of mid-hull over a rear engine deck, its base centred about 0.23 of the hull length ahead of the middle
In travel the six containers lie on the turret with their noses forward against the radar's back face, about x 2.3 m and z 3.3 m (old world point [0.05, 0, 2.96] m)

overlays.note: No drawing of the Buk-M3 exists free; the-blueprints.com sells vectors only. No generated view was made: the open questions are the layout and the length, and a generated view would guess both.

notes.frame_part: the launcher pivot and muzzle (fix), and the mobility and length (unresolved)
notes.why: Beyond detail, the layout is wrong: the model draws a crew cab at the front and the launcher on a turret at the rear; the real 9A317M has no cab, a large forward turret carrying the radar in front and the six-container launcher behind it, and a low engine deck at the rear. Slice 24's buk.py rebuilds the layout first, then adds the radar, rails and fittings.

findings: The Buk-M3 extends roster_profile_wheeled_ifv, so the simulation drives it on wheels; the real vehicle and its art are tracked (GM-569 chassis, track_gauge 0.75 in assets/catalog.json). Changing the mobility profile is a gameplay change outside the frame survey; once tracked, its 4.876 m half-length breaks the 4.8 m tracked cap and must drop (9.3 m suggested). Named for the coordinator.
